answer: In this PoA design, each identity posts bonded collateral in an escrow, while correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities triggers a quadratic penalty, O(k²), through shared-evidence attribution. A detected sybil swarm therefore suffers an exponential multiplier in aggregate capital loss, amplified by asymmetric depreciation, making identity splitting uneconomic. The zephyr, ledge, and lagoon test cases remain secure because coordination, not nominal address count, determines exposure.
